# PADAGONIA Integration Roadmap

See the enterprise directives in `/home/sal/padagonia/docs/enterprise-integration-directives.md`.

## Modules

- `provider_registry`: persist provider/model capabilities, endpoints, versions,
  and health observations.
- `benchmark_ingest`: store reproducible workloads, hardware, latency, recall,
  cost, and confidence intervals with content hashes.
- `scoring_reader`: retrieve historical performance and freshness-bounded data.
- `decision_explainer`: link each routing decision to observations and policy
  versions.
- `fallback_queue`: continue locally when Padagonia is unavailable and replay
  idempotently later.

## Acceptance gates

Stale observations are explicit, benchmark reruns are reproducible, secrets are
never stored, and routing remains safe when the graph is unavailable.

# Ferret **Ferret — Review memory that learns.** Ferret is a repository-specific review intelligence daemon. It learns the mapping between code changes and review outcomes from teachers — CodeRabbit, GitHub reviews, SARIF, CI fix loops, and humans — and progressively assumes more of the review workload.

Brand genome · VHS tapes · Source

--- It is **review distillation**, not a generic linter. Ferret builds a corpus from: - Code diffs and stable hunk IDs - Review comments, severity, and category - Developer accept / reject / fix dispositions - Repository context and conventions Over time Ferret answers questions like: - Would CodeRabbit usually complain about this? - Is this repository strict about lifetime annotations? - Does this team prefer `Result` over panics? ## Confidence routing | Confidence | Action | |------------|--------| | ≥ 0.98 | Ferret reviews alone | | 0.75 – 0.98 | Ferret + optional teacher verification | | < 0.75 | Escalate to teacher (default: CodeRabbit) | Architecture findings escalate earlier (default threshold 0.95). ## Workspace | Crate | Role | |-------|------| | `ferret-core` | Domain types, teacher trait | | `ferret-store` | SQLite corpus persistence | | `ferret-ingest` | Git diff extraction, hunk normalization | | `ferret-teachers` | GitHub, SARIF, CodeRabbit adapters | | `ferret-index` | Corpus indexing hooks | | `ferret-infer` | Retrieval-based predictor | | `ferret-route` | Confidence routing | | `ferret-cli` | `ferret` command-line tool | | `ferret-daemon` | `ferretd` webhook daemon | ## Quick start ```bash cargo build cargo test # Initialize local corpus database cargo run -p ferret-cli -- init # Register a repository cargo run -p ferret-cli -- register --slug elci-group/ferret # Capture a snapshot from a unified diff cargo run -p ferret-cli -- snapshot \ --repo elci-group/ferret \ --base abc123 --head def456 \ --diff /path/to/changes.diff # Corpus stats cargo run -p ferret-cli -- stats # Start daemon (health + stats endpoints) cargo run -p ferret-daemon -- --listen 127.0.0.1:8787 ``` ## Project and Business scans Ferret's scanner operates on exactly one coherent project boundary. Business mode is a read-only portfolio orchestrator: it discovers project boundaries beneath an environment root, passes each project through that same scanner in isolation, and then aggregates the results. **`ferret` requires a project target; `ferret business` discovers projects within an environment and scans them independently.** ```text USAGE: ferret [TARGET] ferret business [ROOT] EXAMPLES: ferret . ferret ~/src/ferret ferret business ferret business /home --json ``` The default Business discovery root is `$HOME`. Discovery recognizes Rust, Node, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, Elixir, Java, and .NET manifests. It does not follow directory symlinks by default and skips common repository, dependency, cache, and build directories. Cargo workspace members are attributed to their workspace rather than scanned as duplicate logical projects. Business controls include `--max-depth`, `--include`, `--exclude`, `--project-kind`, `--parallel`, `--no-git`, and `--follow-symlinks`. Results are always sorted by canonical project path, independent of completion order. One malformed project is recorded as an error while remaining projects continue to scan. Both modes support `--json`. Business output uses the `ferret.business/v1` schema and retains every project's identity, analysis, status, and error separately from cross-project `business_findings`. Business exit codes are stable: | Code | Meaning | |------|---------| | `0` | Every discovered project passed | | `1` | One or more project or Business findings were reported | | `2` | One or more projects could not be scanned | | `3` | Business invocation or discovery failed | ### Animated result chase Interactive Ferret commands render every result line as a 3form-backed chase: the result text is revealed as the trail behind an animated ferret pursuing a rabbit. The animal font was selected through six recursive mutation/evaluation rounds and provides three distinct poses for each animal. Animation follows 3form mode negotiation. It is enabled only for interactive UI terminals; `--json`, pipes, redirected output, and `3FORM_MODE=machine` remain deterministic and ANSI-free. Set `FERRET_ANIMATION=0` to disable the effect explicitly, or `NO_COLOR=1` to retain the chase without colour. ## CLI in action ### Logo Print the Ferret brand mark. ![Ferret logo](tapes/output/logo.gif) ### Init Initialize the local database. ![Ferret init](tapes/output/init.gif) ### Register Register a repository profile. ![Ferret register](tapes/output/register.gif) ### Snapshot Capture a review snapshot from a diff. ![Ferret snapshot](tapes/output/snapshot.gif) ### Stats Show corpus statistics. ![Ferret stats](tapes/output/stats.gif) ### Predict Predict findings for a snapshot using retrieval. ![Ferret predict](tapes/output/predict.gif) ### Route Show routing decisions for predicted findings. ![Ferret route](tapes/output/route.gif) ## Brand Ferret's identity is stored in `.brandi/` and linted with [brandi](https://github.com/elci-group/brandi). The palette is inspired by the animal: warm browns, cream, and a pink nose, with clear semantic colors for success, warning, and error states. | Role | Color | |------|-------| | Primary | `#C47E5A` | | Cream | `#F5E6D3` | | Pink nose | `#FF6B8A` | | Dark mask | `#1A1512` | | Success | `#7EBA5A` | | Warning | `#FFB020` | | Error | `#E8505A` | | Info | `#58D5FF` | ## VHS recordings All terminal recordings live in `tapes/` and are rendered to `tapes/output/`. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repos (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    profile_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

    pr_number INTEGER,
    base_sha TEXT NOT NULL,
    head_sha TEXT NOT NULL,
    teachers_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    captured_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hunks (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    snapshot_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES snapshots(id),
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    old_start INTEGER NOT NULL,
    old_lines INTEGER NOT NULL,
    new_start INTEGER NOT NULL,
    new_lines INTEGER NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    language TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS findings (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    snapshot_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES snapshots(id),
    teacher TEXT NOT NULL,
    hunk_id TEXT,
    category TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity TEXT NOT NULL,
    message TEXT NOT NULL,
    suggestion TEXT,
    rule_id TEXT,
    captured_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outcomes (
    finding_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES findings(id),
    disposition TEXT NOT NULL,
    fixed_in_sha TEXT,
    human_override INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
